Ezra 8:31: On the twelfth day of the first month we set out from the Ahava Canal to go to Jerusalem, and the hand of our God was upon us to protect us from the hands of the enemies and bandits along the way.
Ezra 8:32: So we arrived at Jerusalem and rested there for three days.
>> Ezra 8:33: On the fourth day, in the house of our God, we weighed out the silver and gold and sacred articles into the hand of Meremoth son of Uriah, the priest. Eleazar son of Phinehas was with him, along with the Levites Jozabad son of Jeshua and Noadiah son of Binnui.
Ezra 8:34: Everything was verified by number and weight, and the total weight was recorded at that time.
Ezra 8:35: Then the exiles who had returned from captivity sacrificed burnt offerings to the God of Israel: 12 bulls for all Israel, 96 rams, 77 lambs, and a sin offering of 12 male goats. All this was a burnt offering to the LORD.
Ezra 8:36: They also delivered the king's edicts to the royal satraps and governors of the region west of the Euphrates, who proceeded to assist the people and the house of God.

first.why: The verses state they were present with the priest, but do not state that they carried the offering.

a.why: the three are named as receivers of the weighed silver and gold, not as carriers (Ezra 8:33)

b.why: Ezra 8:33: Eleazar, Jozabad and Noadiah receive the weighed silver, gold and articles; the priests and Levites carried them (8:30)

rows.claim: CLAIM Herod - died at - Caesarea.
rows.verse:
Acts 12:16: But Peter kept on knocking, and when they opened the door and saw him, they were astounded.
Acts 12:17: Peter motioned with his hand for silence, and he described how the Lord had brought him out of the prison. “Send word to James and to the brothers,” he said, and he left for another place.
Acts 12:18: At daybreak there was no small commotion among the soldiers as to what had become of Peter.
>> Acts 12:19: After Herod had searched for him unsuccessfully, he examined the guards and ordered that they be executed. Then he went down from Judea to Caesarea and spent some time there.
Acts 12:20: Now Herod was in a furious dispute with the people of Tyre and Sidon, and they convened before him. Having secured the support of Blastus, the king's chamberlain, they asked for peace, because their region depended on the king's country for food.
Acts 12:21: On the appointed day, Herod donned his royal robes, sat on his throne, and addressed the people.
Acts 12:22: And they began to shout, “This is the voice of a god, not a man!”

first.why: The verse says he went to Caesarea and spent time there, but it does not say he died there.

a.why: he goes to Caesarea and stays there; his death is not reported in this passage (Acts 12:19-22)

b.why: Acts 12:19-22 only shows Herod going to Caesarea and speaking; his death is not in this passage (Acts 12:23)

rows.claim: CLAIM Abraham - went to - Haran.
rows.verse:
Gen 12:1: Then the LORD said to Abram, “Leave your country, your kindred, and your father's household, and go to the land I will show you.
Gen 12:2: I will make you into a great nation, and I will bless you; I will make your name great, so that you will be a blessing.
Gen 12:3: I will bless those who bless you and curse those who curse you; and all the families of the earth will be blessed through you.”
>> Gen 12:4: So Abram departed, as the LORD had directed him, and Lot went with him. Abram was seventy-five years old when he left Haran.
Gen 12:5: And Abram took his wife Sarai, his nephew Lot, and all the possessions and people they had acquired in Haran, and set out for the land of Canaan. When they came to the land of Canaan,
Gen 12:6: Abram traveled through the land as far as the site of the Oak of Moreh at Shechem. And at that time the Canaanites were in the land.
Gen 12:7: Then the LORD appeared to Abram and said, “I will give this land to your offspring.” So Abram built an altar there to the LORD, who had appeared to him.

first.why: The verse states he left Haran, not that he went to it.

a.why: Haran is where he left from; he set out for Canaan (Gen 12:4-5)

b.why: Gen 12:4: Abram left Haran; going to Haran is Gen 11:31, outside this passage

rows.claim: CLAIM David - blessed - the kingdom of Israel under Saul, David and Solomon.
rows.verse:
1Chr 16:1: So they brought the ark of God and placed it inside the tent that David had pitched for it. And they presented burnt offerings and peace offerings before God.
>> 1Chr 16:2: When David had finished sacrificing the burnt offerings and peace offerings, he blessed the people in the name of the LORD.
1Chr 16:3: Then he distributed to every man and woman of Israel a loaf of bread, a date cake, and a raisin cake.
1Chr 16:4: David appointed some of the Levites to minister before the ark of the LORD, to celebrate, to give thanks, and to praise the LORD, the God of Israel.
1Chr 16:5: Asaph was the chief, Zechariah was second, then Jeiel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Mattithiah, Eliab, Benaiah, Obed-edom, and Jeiel. They were to play the harps and lyres, while Asaph sounded the cymbals

first.words: he blessed the people in the name of the LORD
first.why: The verse says David blessed the people, not the kingdom itself.

a.why: he blessed the assembled people, not the kingdom spanning three reigns (1Chr 16:2-3)

b.why: 1 Chr 16:2: David blessed the assembled people of Israel, not a kingdom spanning Saul, David and Solomon

rows.claim: CLAIM Hanun - attacked - David.
rows.verse:
1Chr 19:1: Some time later, Nahash king of the Ammonites died and was succeeded by his son.
1Chr 19:2: And David said, “I will show kindness to Hanun son of Nahash, because his father showed kindness to me.” So David sent messengers to console Hanun concerning his father. But when David's servants arrived in the land of the Ammonites to console him,
1Chr 19:3: the princes of the Ammonites said to Hanun, “Just because David has sent you comforters, do you really believe he is showing respect for your father? Have not his servants come to you to explore the land, spy it out, and overthrow it?”
>> 1Chr 19:4: So Hanun took David's servants, shaved their beards, cut off their garments at the hips, and sent them away.
1Chr 19:5: When someone came and told David about his men, he sent messengers to meet them, since the men had been thoroughly humiliated. The king told them, “Stay in Jericho until your beards have grown back, and then return.”
>> 1Chr 19:6: When the Ammonites realized that they had become a stench to David, Hanun and the Ammonites sent a thousand talents of silver to hire for themselves chariots and horsemen from Aram-naharaim, Aram-maacah, and Zobah.
1Chr 19:7: So they hired for themselves thirty-two thousand chariots, as well as the king of Maacah with his troops, who came and camped near Medeba while the Ammonites were mustered from their cities and marched out for battle.
1Chr 19:8: On hearing this, David sent Joab and the entire army of mighty men.
1Chr 19:9: The Ammonites marched out and arrayed themselves for battle at the entrance to the city, while the kings who had come stayed by themselves in the open country.

first.why: The verses describe Hanun humiliating David's servants and preparing for war, but they do not state that he attacked David himself.

a.why: Hanun humiliated David's envoys and hired chariots; no attack on David (1Chr 19:4-6)

b.why: 1 Chr 19:4-9: Hanun shaves and expels David's envoys, then hires chariots and musters; no attack on David

rows.claim: CLAIM Barnabas - went to - Perga.
rows.verse:
Acts 14:17: Yet He has not left Himself without testimony to His goodness: He gives you rain from heaven and fruitful seasons, filling your hearts with food and gladness.”
Acts 14:18: Even with these words, Paul and Barnabas could hardly stop the crowds from sacrificing to them.
Acts 14:19: Then some Jews arrived from Antioch and Iconium and won over the crowds. They stoned Paul and dragged him outside the city, presuming he was dead.
>> Acts 14:20: But after the disciples had gathered around him, he got up and went back into the city. And the next day he left with Barnabas for Derbe.
Acts 14:21: They preached the gospel to that city and made many disciples. Then they returned to Lystra, Iconium, and Antioch,
Acts 14:22: strengthening the souls of the disciples and encouraging them to continue in the faith. “We must endure many hardships to enter the kingdom of God,” they said.
Acts 14:23: Paul and Barnabas appointed elders for them in each church, praying and fasting as they entrusted them to the Lord, in whom they had believed.

first.why: The verses state he left with Barnabas for Derbe, but do not mention them going to Perga.

a.why: Barnabas left with Paul for Derbe (14:20) and returned to Lystra, Iconium, Antioch (14:21); Perga is not named anywhere in the passage.

b.why: Perga is not in this passage; they left for Derbe (14:20) and returned to Lystra, Iconium, Antioch (14:21)

rows.claim: CLAIM Hathach - charged - Mordecai.
rows.verse:
Esth 4:3: In every province to which the king's command and edict came, there was great mourning among the Jews. They fasted, wept, and lamented, and many lay in sackcloth and ashes.
Esth 4:4: When Esther's maidens and eunuchs came and told her about Mordecai, the queen was overcome with distress. She sent clothes for Mordecai to wear instead of his sackcloth, but he would not accept them.
Esth 4:5: Then Esther summoned Hathach, one of the king's eunuchs appointed to her, and she dispatched him to Mordecai to learn what was troubling him and why.
>> Esth 4:6: So Hathach went out to Mordecai in the city square in front of the king's gate,
Esth 4:7: and Mordecai told him all that had happened to him, including the exact amount of money that Haman had promised to pay into the royal treasury in order to destroy the Jews.
Esth 4:8: Mordecai also gave Hathach a copy of the written decree issued in Susa for the destruction of the Jews, to show and explain to Esther, urging her to approach the king, implore his favor, and plead before him for her people.
>> Esth 4:9: So Hathach went back and relayed Mordecai's response to Esther.
Esth 4:10: Then Esther spoke to Hathach and instructed him to tell Mordecai,
Esth 4:11: “All the royal officials and the people of the king's provinces know that one law applies to every man or woman who approaches the king in the inner court without being summoned-that he be put to death. Only if the king extends the gold scepter may that person live. But I have not been summoned to appear before the king for the past thirty days.”
Esth 4:12: When Esther's words were relayed to Mordecai,

first.why: The verses describe Hathach delivering messages to and from Mordecai, but they do not state that he charged him with anything.

a.why: Charge runs the other way: Mordecai gave Hathach the decree and the urging for Esther (4:8), Esther instructed Hathach (4:10); Hathach only went and relayed (4:6, 4:9).

b.why: Hathach is the messenger: Esther dispatched and instructed him (4:5, 4:10); he relayed words both ways, he did not charge Mordecai
